summary: During the requested investigation window, checkout-service resident memory rose 2.0x, from 628.36 MiB to 1230.67 MiB. Logs also show repeated warnings of 92% heap usage with GC overhead approaching its limit, followed by Java heap-space OutOfMemoryError occurrences. This supports JVM heap exhaustion as the immediate failure mechanism, but the evidence does not establish why heap usage grew or identify a specific code, deployment, or traffic cause.

likely_causes.title: Sustained JVM heap pressure culminating in heap exhaustion
likely_causes.rationale: Repeated high-heap and GC-overhead warnings alongside Java heap-space errors support heap exhaustion as the immediate cause of the observed memory issue. The evidence does not distinguish a memory leak or retained objects from other application or workload behavior.

supporting_evidence.detail: 17 WARN documents reported “GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92%”; warning samples span 2026-10-26T14:22:32Z to 2026-10-26T15:38:32Z.
5 ERROR documents reported “java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space”; error samples span 2026-10-26T15:16:32Z to 2026-10-26T15:38:32Z.
Threshold-validated resident-memory metric rose 2.0x, from 628.36 MiB to 1230.67 MiB; anomaly_detected=True.

next_steps: Capture and analyze a heap dump or allocation profile under elevated heap usage to identify dominant objects and retention paths.
Review JVM heap and GC telemetry, including allocation rate, post-GC live set, and collection behavior.
Compare memory behavior across deployments and inspect relevant changes; the evidence does not establish that version v1.4.2 caused the issue.
Check request-rate and workload measurements before assessing traffic as a contributor; no request-rate evidence was provided.
Confirm metric and log coverage across the requested interval; the findings do not establish continuous data coverage.
